rounds.text: Aditya Infotech Ltd is exhibiting extraordinary growth momentum that easily justifies strong market attention, anchored by a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 65% [E16] and a staggering trailing twelve-month profit growth of 212% [E19]. The underlying profitability of the business is exceptional, evidenced by a robust ROCE of 28.6% [E12] and consistent multi-year return on equity figures sitting at a median of 28% over five years [E21] and 26% over three years [E22]. Furthermore, institutional confidence is unmistakably shifting in our favor, marked by positive institutional money flow (+2.94 percentage points) [E38] driven by significant accumulation from both foreign and domestic institutions over the past year [E36, E37]. Operational capability is also scaling up efficiently, as demonstrated by a shrinking Capital Work in Progress (CWIP) down 51.2% year-on-year, signaling that new capacity is rapidly coming online [E34] to support a broader sector tailwind in Capital Goods with a positive tailwind score of +0.59 [E69]. Conceded: the valuation metrics indicate a high entry barrier with a P/E ratio of 78.7 [E1], a price-to-book ratio of 13.25 [E2], and a discounted cash flow model showing a negative margin of safety [E40].

The current valuation of Aditya Infotech Ltd is detached from fundamental intrinsic value, with a discounted cash flow model placing intrinsic value at Rs 1969 per share against a market price of Rs 3963, resulting in a severe negative margin of safety of -101.2% [E39, E40]. This excessive price leaves no margin for error, as the stock trades at an exorbitant P/E of 78.7x and a price-to-book ratio of 13.25x, which vastly exceeds sector benchmarks of 22.02x and 2.4x respectively [E1, E2, E6, E7]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's market price already prices in an aggressive 27.8% earnings growth rate, surpassing the 18.0% growth assumed in the base case [E41]. Operational quality also fails to justify these multiples, evidenced by a dismal cash conversion ratio of 0.04x for March 2026 where profits far outstrip actual operating cash flow, alongside negative free cash flow of Rs -120 Cr [E28, E30]. Working capital pressures are mounting with working capital days expanding from 40.8 to 73.9 days [E58], and borrowings have escalated to Rs 417 Cr in September 2026 up from Rs 256 Cr a year prior [E33]. Conceded: [E39, E40]. While the DCF and valuation multiples look demanding, the bear completely overlooks the exceptional fundamental momentum that easily justifies a premium [E1, E2, E6, E7]. Compounded profit growth stands at a staggering 66% over 5 years and reached 212% in the trailing twelve months, demonstrating that earnings are scaling far faster than standard historical baselines assume [E17, E19]. Operating margins have expanded by 8 percentage points in the TTM period to reach 16% and hit 17% in September 2026, proving that business profitability is structurally improving rather than stagnating [E24, E25]. Furthermore, institutional confidence is surging with positive money flow and major accumulation from foreign and domestic institutions pushing institutional holdings up by 2.94 percentage points [E38]. Finally, the Capital Goods sector is firmly in a tailwind with a score of +0.59, and the company's rules-based screen score of 86 out of 100 with a BUY rating confirms that the operational reality outweighs static valuation models [E59, E67].

Conceded: [E17, E19, E24, E25, E38]. While profit growth and margins have expanded, this high growth is already fully priced in and masks severe cash generation failures [E28, E30, E66]. The valuation multiples are extreme, with a P/E of 78.7x and a P/B of 13.25x that vastly exceed sector benchmarks of 22.02x and 2.4x respectively [E1, E2, E6, E7]. The business shows a dangerous divergence between accounting profits and actual cash: cash conversion is a meagre 0.04x, resulting in negative free cash flow of Rs -120 Cr as working capital days balloon from 40.8 to 73.9 days [E28, E30, E58]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price requires an aggressive 27.8% earnings growth, even higher than the base case's 18.0% assumption [E41]. Compounding these risks, earnings growth is actively decelerating according to screening flags while promoter holdings continue to decline [E35, E57, E64].

Conceded: [E28, E30, E58]. While cash conversion and free cash flow require close monitoring as working capital days expand, the bear ignores the extraordinary top-and-bottom line velocity driving this business [E16, E19]. Compounded sales growth reached 65% in the trailing twelve months while compounded profit growth soared by 212%, outperforming sector medians by a wide margin [E16, E19, E70, E71]. This fundamental acceleration is validated by institutional accumulation, with foreign and domestic institutions increasing their stakes and creating positive money flow of +2.94 percentage points [E36, E37, E38]. Furthermore, the company operates with a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.11x alongside declining capital work-in-progress, indicating that completed capex is poised to bring fresh capacity online [E31, E34]. The robust momentum is underpinned by a sector tailwind score of +0.59 in Capital Goods, propelling the stock's relative-strength rating to a maximum of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E45, E67].

Conceded: [E16, E19, E36, E37, E38, E45]. While the bull highlights exceptional trailing sales and profit velocities alongside institutional accumulation and maximum relative strength, this fundamental acceleration masks severe cash disconnects and overextended valuation multiples [E16, E19, E36, E37, E38, E45]. The massive profit surge fails to translate into actual liquidity, evidenced by a dismal cash conversion ratio of 0.04x and a plunging free cash flow of Rs -120 Cr as working capital days expand from 40.8 to 73.9 days [E28, E30, E58]. Furthermore, the bull's emphasis on conservative debt is undermined by actual borrowings expanding from Rs 256 Cr to Rs 417 Cr year-over-year [E33]. The current price trades at an extreme P/E of 78.7x and a price-to-book of 13.25x, which vastly outpaces sector benchmarks and leaves a negative DCF margin of safety of -101.2% [E1, E2, E6, E7, E40]. Finally, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price already demands an unrealistic 27.8% earnings growth rate, proving that the market has already aggressively priced in the bull's entire growth narrative [E41].
